title: How I lost $1M+ in niche site value to Google updates, and what I'd do differently
summary: Jacky Chou openly reports his lows: about $1.4M of niche site value went to zero in 2024 after Google updates hit his ecom brand Farway and several sites sharing one Search Console account. His main lesson is to stop talking publicly about a site once it hits meaningful revenue. He also explains why the public posting still paid off through partnership deals.

principles.text: If you report your highs publicly, report your lows too. Honest reporting builds credibility.
principles.quote: I'm a firm believer that if you can report the highs you got to report the lows as well

principles.text: Stop publicly talking about a site once it hits meaningful revenue; attention can attract scrutiny.
principles.quote: I think in hindsight I should have stopped talking about far and away after it hit certain Revenue s like thresholds I should have just stopped mentioning it all

principles.text: Don't keep several sites in the same Google Search Console account; a penalty on one can drag the others down.
principles.quote: it was in the same Google Search Console account in hindsight stupid right

principles.text: Don't ignore small assets just because a bigger one pays more. Small sites carry real value and can be lost too.
principles.quote: I didn't care cuz my Partnerships were making freaking 500k a month why would I care right it was totaling only 20K a month

principles.text: Building in public can snowball. Posting openly about a site brought partnership deals, and being known for partnerships brought inbound brands.
principles.quote: me posting so highly openly about farway got me my first couple partnership deals and with that I was able to run it up to like C couple Mill in profit this year

principles.text: Know when to go quiet while the money is good. Hype and disclosure carry risk.
principles.quote: I think I did most things right I think I just should have just shut up when money was good
